key_insight: DK-VLM improves spatial reasoning in vision-language models by treating geometry as a form of position, so the model can better understand 3D relations across views and update them as the observer moves.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty vision-language models have in reasoning about 3D spatial relationships across different viewpoints, especially when limited spatial supervision makes it hard to align reconstructed geometry with pretrained semantic features.
method: Introduces Dual-Kernel Attention, which combines attention based on a token's original visual position and its geometric position in the scene.
Integrates 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens while improving alignment with semantic representations.
Uses geometry-aware spatial modeling to support more consistent spatial judgments across changing viewpoints.
impact: This matters for AI practitioners building multimodal systems that need robust spatial understanding, such as robotics, embodied AI, AR/VR, and scene reasoning applications. It offers a practical way to strengthen 3D-aware reasoning without relying entirely on dense spatial supervision.

paper_title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Han Su, Meng Tian, Tianyu Huang, Mingyu Gao, Lennox Wei
